name: ThriveCart
tagline: Checkout pages, funnels, subscriptions, affiliates, and course delivery

pricing.notes: The pricing model is not safely comparable as one fixed monthly USD amount. Review the official source before publication.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: Unlimited products, funnels, courses, and students; 1 order bump; 2,000 community members; 10 communities; 100 GB hosted video; 2 GB per video; 1080p

tiers.name: Pro+
tiers.limits: Unlimited products, courses, and students; multiple order bumps; 10,000 community members; unlimited communities; 500 GB hosted video; 4 GB per video; 1080p; custom domain

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom scale, support, and service limits

tiers.name: Standard Lifetime
tiers.notes: A separate optional Pro+ upgrade is $295/year.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 30-day trial on subscription plans
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; separate $495 one-time lifetime licence with optional $295/year Pro+ upgrade
pricing.hiddenCosts: The lifetime purchase does not include Pro+ permanently: keeping the optional Pro+ upgrade costs $295/year. External payment processors still charge their own processing fees.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. ThriveCart's durable value is payments, network, compliance, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a narrow checkout platform storefront or member area for one creator, using Stripe Checkout and explicit digital-delivery rules.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: Stripe account and API keys in .env
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: tax, disputes, payouts, and fraud operations
whyPeopleStillPay: ThriveCart: Creators pay to outsource payments, tax complexity, disputes, deliverability, moderation, and the trust needed to convert strangers.
ongoingBurden: Own payments, webhooks, refunds, tax records, fraud, access control, file delivery, moderation, backups, and support.

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: Checkout pages, bumps, upsells, subscriptions, one affiliate program and one course on a real free plan.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Ghost
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A membership publisher is not a checkout-funnel and affiliate platform.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Medusa
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Commerce plumbing for developers, not a ready-made checkout, funnel and course business.

rejectedAlternatives.name: WooCommerce
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Checkout exists; free subscriptions, funnels, affiliates and course delivery do not arrive together.

notes: Credibility row: ThriveCart survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by ThriveCart; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL + Stripe.
Primary job: Build a narrow checkout platform storefront or member area for one creator, using Stripe Checkout and explicit digital-delivery rules.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: marketplace discovery and buyer trust; tax, disputes, payouts, and fraud operations; native apps and community moderation.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
